comment.narrative: Baseline Afghanistan focusing only on NGOs support UNODC IOM and UNHCR Iraq ongoing GLO.ACT Asia and the Middle East Pakistan ongoing GLO.ACT Asia and the Middle East Central Asia NA.
At least two new initiatives.

Since inception 2 stakeholders have supported through grants to provide direct assistance. During the reporting period Afghanistan YHDO reached and assisted 14529 individuals 7515 female7014 maleInformation Education and Communications IEC flyers were distributed to 3933 target beneficiaries 2097 female1836 male. The IEC materials focused on the risks of TIP and SOM and its prevention.Psychosocial counselling services were provided to a total of 3411 target individuals 1700female1711 male. 2313 beneficiaries 1092 female1221 male were provided by Kandahar DIC with basic social services and education on the risks associated with drug use and TIP and SOM methods for prevention.2457 beneficiaries 1317 female1140 male were provided with Voluntary Confidential Counselling and Testing VCCT services covering HIV HBS HCV and Syphilis. This service is crucial for people who are concerned about their HIV status but may feel hesitant to get tested due to fear of stigmatization or discrimination.2415 individuals 1309 female1106 male received primary health care services.DCA Work postponed due to the change in livestock price. The project budget was revised with a topup of 40000 USD and timeline of five months JuneOctober 2024 to ensure more beneficiaries will be reached .Tajikistan UNODC presented at the official opening of phase II of the MRC Tajikistan and MRC Tajikistan strategic planning workshop . November 2023 Note This output currently only relates to work undertaken in Afghanistan.
